newsitem.title: USA: Louis Dreyfus sees production rise through 1997.
newsitem.headline: Louis Dreyfus sees production rise through 1997.

text.p: Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp said on Tuesday that its hydrocarbon production should increase through the balance of the year, buoyed by recent successes completions of development wells.

The company, in a report accompanying its financial results for the second quarter, said that for the first six months of 1997, it successfully completed 94 percent of its development wells and over 80 percent of its exploratory wells.
It said it currently has 14 rigs presently drilling and plans to drill 180 additional wells by yearend.
The company said total hydrocarbon production for the quarter ended June 30, 1997, was 18.6 billion cubic feet equivalent (BCFE), compared with 19.2 (BCFE) produced during the second quarter of 1996.
Gas production for the second quarter of 1997 was 16.1 billion cubic feet (BCF), compared to l6.4 (BCF) produced in the second quarter of l996, it said.
Oil production for the second quarter of 1997 decreased to 414,000 barrels of oil compared to 466,000 barrels for the second quarter of 1996, it said.
The decline in oil production was primarily the result of the sale of a non-core West Texas waterflood property in the first quarter of 1997, it said.
At the same time, Mark Monroe, president and chief executive officer, said the company looks forward to its merger with American Exploration Co.

He said plans are being refined by the management teams of both companies to permit an expeditious and orderly transition upon a favorable shareholder vote of the proposed merger, which was announced on June 24.
